name: Sales Pipeline - ETL to BigQuery to Forecast (Hostinger VPS via SSH)

nodes.name: SSH: Simulate New Daily Transactions
nodes.notes: This is a portfolio-project device: since this dataset is historical and static (2022-2025, no live feed), this step generates one statistically-realistic new day of transactions (sampled from the real historical distributions) and appends it to the raw CSV, so the daily pipeline has something genuinely new to process each run. In a real deployment this node would be replaced by whatever actually produces new transactions (a POS system export, an orders API, etc.).

parameters.command: cd /root/return-risk-pipeline && source venv/bin/activate && python3 etl/clean.py --input data/raw/Sales_transactions_2022_2025.csv --output data/processed/sales_clean.csv --report data/processed/data_quality_report.json

nodes.name: SSH: Run ETL (clean.py)
nodes.notes: Runs on the VPS host, NOT inside the n8n Docker container. Assumes the repo is at /root/return-risk-pipeline and a venv with requirements.txt already installed. Swap the credential for whichever SSH credential you create in n8n (password or private key).

parameters.command: cd /root/return-risk-pipeline && source venv/bin/activate && export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/root/gcp-key.json && python3 etl/load_bigquery.py --project bigqueryproject-509014 --dataset sales_analytics

nodes.name: SSH: Load to BigQuery
nodes.notes: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS points at the service account key file already placed on the VPS (uploaded via SFTP, never committed to git). Replace GCP_PROJECT_ID with your actual project id, either hardcoded here or set as an n8n environment variable and referenced via an expression.

parameters.command: cd /root/return-risk-pipeline && source venv/bin/activate && python3 models/forecast.py --data data/processed/sales_clean.csv --model_dir models/artifacts

meta.description: Daily orchestration for n8n self-hosted on a Hostinger VPS (Docker). Uses SSH nodes (not Execute Command) because the n8n container itself doesn't have Python/the repo installed — commands run on the VPS host instead, where you set up a venv with requirements.txt. Before importing: (1) create an SSH credential in n8n pointed at your VPS, (2) replace REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_SSH_CREDENTIAL_ID in each SSH node with that credential's id, (3) confirm the repo path (/root/return-risk-pipeline) matches where you actually placed it, (4) set GCP_PROJECT_ID either hardcoded in the BigQuery node's command or as an n8n environment variable.
